Первые портреты по способу «Глубокий промт персонажа» (art/style/style.md): кто он и чего хочет сейчас · характер в лице и осанке · поза словами в миг действия · пять личных деталей из глав · место. Слова автора 29.09.2026: «больше пафоса… поза… детали, связанные с личностью… портрет отражал характер». Рецепт принятых портретов (jobs/heroes-batch-02.json): тот же стиль и три референса стиля из art/style; кадр — по пояс, корпус вправо, к врагам, камера теперь чуть снизу. Редкость не рисуем, класс — по оружию или действию, школа — по цвету света. У Ветверога без ref-04: на нём зверь, модель перерисовала бы его. Источники: docs/content/герои/состав-героев.csv, главы/цикл-1.md, лор-аудит.md. Детали, которых нет в главах, — решение агента, по строке в source
style: Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, heroic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — crystals and cracks that glow from within — throw colored light upward, the light comes from below. Cold and warm light contrast. Dust motes and grains of sand float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime. Match the brushwork, lighting and color handling of the attached style reference images, but do NOT copy their subjects, objects, letters or composition.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no real-world alphabets, no runes or markings that look like writing, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture, no gems or badges of rank. No bodies, no skulls, no blood. Only one character in the foreground; a person has exactly two arms and two hands. Not stiff, not passive, not posing like a mannequin; no empty eyes.

heroes.frame: Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Format: vertical hero card portrait, 4:5. A close, heroic half-body portrait from the waist or hips up, three-quarter view; no knees, no legs, no feet in the frame. The camera is a little below the hero's chest and looks slightly up, so the hero towers — a legend, not an extra. The hero's body is turned toward the right side of the picture, toward unseen enemies beyond the right edge, and the face is seen in three-quarter view looking to the right. The hero is caught at the peak of an action that shows who they are; the pose carries weight and intent. Head in the upper third, the face large, well lit and readable at small size, with a clear expression; the lower quarter may be darker because the card puts the name there. Rich atmospheric background that tells where the hero lived, with depth and soft focus, darker than the character. Light comes from below and from glowing crystals; rim light separates the figure from the background.

jobs.subject: Subject: Astrid Half-Grosh, a woman of the northern lands, a warrior of great strength of the Fire school. Who she is: of the northern women, only three in a generation go to the arena sands and on campaigns, and the north knew her by her second blade — a fire stone was set into it when she was twenty. On the campaign against the southern elven forest the jarl gave her the purse of the campaign: the second halves of split coins for the hired strangers, who had taken the first halves in advance. On the third day the forest paths began to go in circles. She was afraid, like everyone — and she went on. Character: steadfast, honest and fierce; fear burned away by fire, duty kept to the last. Her face: early thirties, weathered and freckled, a strong jaw, a thin white scar across one cheekbone, fierce grey eyes with the scarlet glow of the stone reflected in them, lips drawn back over gritted teeth in a battle cry; ash-blond hair in thick northern braids, a few loose strands whipped by the heat. Pose, the moment of the charge: she charges toward the right, her weight thrown onto her leading shoulder, her torso twisting into the swing. Her near hand holds a broad northern sword low and back, ready to sweep up; her far hand raises the second blade high above her shoulder — a shorter, heavy blade with a scarlet fire stone set at the base of the blade, glowing like a coal, flames licking along its edge (Fire). Her head is lowered, chin tucked, eyes fixed on the enemy beyond the right edge. Details that tell her story: (1) at her belt hangs a heavy leather purse tied tight with a thong, a few dull half-coins with jagged broken edges glinting at its mouth — she never lets go of it; (2) a mail shirt under a sleeveless fur-trimmed leather jerkin, a wide belt; (3) old burn scars on the wrist and forearm of the hand that holds the fire blade; (4) a thin iron torc at her neck; (5) forest mist curling around her and dead leaves torn up by her charge. Place: a dark primeval elven forest where the paths go in circles: colossal twisted trees and huge roots, mist, a path that loops back on itself behind her. Scarlet-red light of the Fire school rises from glowing embers among the roots below and from her blade; cold mist beyond.

jobs.subject_v1: Subject: Eavin the Carver, an elven woman of the southern forest, a swift archer of the Air school. Who she is: a master bowyer who carved bows out of living trees without felling them: she took only as much as the trunk would give, and the tree grew on. That was her key. She had many pupils, but every one of them cut across the grain at least once, so for two hundred years she argued with the elders that a secret is better carried away than left half-kept. Her last bow she carved from the tree under which she asked to be laid. Character: proud, uncompromising and exacting — a master who accepts nothing by halves. Her face: ageless, looking about fifty by human measure, fine lines at the eyes, high sharp cheekbones, long pointed elven ears, a narrow proud mouth; silver-streaked dark hair tied back tightly with a strip of bark; grey-green eyes narrowed along the arrow, cool and certain. Pose, the moment of the shot: she has turned sharply toward the right in one fluid movement and loosed an arrow: her bow arm is fully extended toward the right, the bow canted, the string still quivering; her drawing hand has just released beside her jaw and is opening, fingers spread; her shoulders are square to the shot, her chin raised. A spiral of white-green wind (Air) follows the arrow toward the right edge, tearing leaves and fine wood shavings along with it. Details that tell her story: (1) her bow is living wood: bark still on its back, fine growth rings on its face, and a few young green leaves sprouting from its tips; (2) a crooked carving knife with a worn antler handle hangs at her belt, and curls of pale wood shavings are caught in her sleeves; (3) her fingers are a carver's — callused, with thin white scars, a leather thumb guard on the drawing hand; (4) a sash of woven bast across her chest holds a few arrows fletched with grey feathers; (5) behind her the trunk of a colossal living tree bears a fresh, smooth notch cut exactly to the width of a palm. Place: an ancient elven forest of colossal living trees at dusk. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the mossy roots below and from small crystals among them; leaves and shavings drift in the wind.
jobs.subject: EDIT MODE — this overrides everything above: do not draw a new picture, edit the attached image. The attached image is the current portrait of this hero, Eavin the Carver: an elven woman with grey hair in a bun, drawing a living bow with leaves toward the right in a dark forest. Keep the picture exactly as it is — the same woman, her face, ears, hair, clothes, sash, knife, quiver, arrows, both hands, the bow and its leaves, the string, the arrow, the wind spiral, the crystals, the light, the colors and the painting style. Change only this: behind her, to the right of her waist, there is a pale tree stump with a flat cut top — she never fells trees, so there must be no stump. Remove the stump and paint in its place the dark bark of the great living tree trunk behind her, whole and unbroken. Nothing else changes.

jobs.subject: Subject: Elias, a homeless archer of the roads, a human man, a swift archer of the Air school. Who he is: he guarded caravans for food and never asked where they went. On a southern road he carried a fallen elven wanderer into the shade, and she gave him a scroll that would admit him to the great Tree of the elves. He did not go to the Tree — he went after her. With her small band he walked the old roads, and for the first time he had a home, only it was always on the move. He learned to shoot so quietly that he never woke the sleepers in camp. Character: quiet, restrained and loyal to the end — a man of few words who has found something to protect. His face: in his thirties, lean and weathered, a short dark beard, dark hair tied back, a thin scar through one eyebrow, calm dark eyes utterly focused; his lips pressed together, holding his breath. Pose, the moment before the shot: he stands between the sleeping camp and the dark, his body turned toward the right, and draws a long plain bow to full draw toward the right; the fletching touches the corner of his mouth, the drawing elbow is high behind him, the bow arm straight and steady; his head is tilted slightly to the arrow, eyes on the enemy beyond the right edge. A thin thread of white-green wind (Air) winds silently around the arrowhead. Details that tell his story: (1) a rolled scroll tied with a stem of dry grass is tucked under the strap across his chest, its seal unbroken — he never unrolled it; (2) small tufts of wool are bound onto his bowstring so it makes no sound; (3) a caravan guard's worn leather bracer on his bow arm and a road-worn, much-patched grey cloak; (4) mismatched arrows in his quiver, fletched with feathers of different birds gathered on the road; (5) a bedroll strapped across his back. Place: an ancient paved road at night beside a ruined roadside station of pale stone; behind him, small and warm, a campfire, and around it the dark shapes of his sleeping companions under blankets. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from cracks between the old paving stones below; road dust drifts in the light.

jobs.subject_v1: Subject: Vetverog, a sentient beast of the southern elven forest, a warrior of great strength of the Air school. Who he is: in the elven forest there are beasts that the Watchers raise with a single word. No one ever raised him: he came out to the fire of the two-legged wanderers by himself and lay down beside it — he decided, not the herd. He walked with them to the end, and when the last of them, the archer, was laid by the road, he lay down beside him and went no further. Character: proud, free and loyal by his own choice — a wild lord of the forest with a thinking mind. His eyes are deep amber-gold and intelligent, calm and grave: the eyes of someone who remembers. Appearance: a colossal forest stag-beast, bigger than an elk, with a heavy mane of grey-brown fur on his neck and chest and a crown of enormous antlers that branch like the limbs of an old tree — pale as bone, spreading wide, with moss and a few small living leaves growing on them. Framing and pose, the moment of the charge: he is a beast, so the half-body frame shows his head, antlers, neck, chest and front legs; his hindquarters are out of the frame. The camera is low. He charges toward the right: his head is lowered, the great antlers swept forward like a wall of branches aimed at the enemy beyond the right edge; one foreleg is raised mid-stride, the other drives into the earth; the muscles of his neck bunch under the mane, his nostrils flare, and his breath streams out as white-green wind (Air) that whirls leaves around his antlers. Details that tell his story: (1) a thin braided cord of dry grass is tied around one tine of his antlers — a token from the healer who touched each companion every evening as if counting them; (2) the fur of his chest is darkened with the smoke of many campfires; (3) an old notch in one ear and a pale scar across his muzzle; (4) one antler tine is broken off short and has healed smooth; (5) embers from a campfire drift around him. Place: the edge of an ancient elven forest by a dusty road at dusk, a small campfire glowing behind him. Pale white-green light of the Air school rises from the roots and the earth below; leaves and sparks drift in the air.

jobs.subject_v1: Subject: Oelis the Unlayering, a woman of a forgotten people who lived long before all the cities that stand today, a controller and battle mage of the Time school. Who she is: her people were as many as the stars over the river, and every craft had its own key — not a word, but the way you hold your hand. Her key was to take the years off things, layer by layer, the way bark is peeled, until the new showed through under the old: a cracked wall came out of her hands whole, a black bowl came out bright as on the day it was fired. Their city stood by the water and was built of white clay. Once she was asked to take the years off a person, and she tried — under the years a person has nothing new, only the same, shorter; she pulled her hands back and never tried again. The last thing she renewed was the bowl in which her people's fire burned. Character: grave, sorrowful and unbending — the last of her people, who knows exactly what her power costs and uses it without hesitation. A timeless, majestic presence: a legend. Her face: ageless and striking, unlike any people living now — a long neck, a long narrow face, large heavy-lidded eyes with luminous green irises, warm bronze-brown skin; many thin braids of dark hair bound with small rings of white fired clay; fine lines of white clay painted along her brow and cheekbones. Pose, the moment of the spell: she stands turned toward the right, her head held high, her gaze level and unafraid. Her near hand is thrust out toward the right with the fingers curled as if gripping the edge of something invisible — and she peels it back: from the enemy beyond the right edge long curling layers of pale green light peel away toward her like strips of bark, drifting and dissolving into motes (Time). Her far hand holds a shallow clay bowl close to her chest, and a small flame burns in it. Details that tell her story: (1) the bowl is of white clay, bright and new as on the day it was fired, while its foot is still black and cracked — it is being renewed layer by layer; (2) her hands are dusted with white clay up to the wrists; (3) a robe of undyed pale linen with a wide collar of white clay beads and small river shells; (4) a small whistle of bone hangs on a cord at her throat; (5) the hem of her sleeves frays into fine pale flakes that curl and drift away like peeled layers. Place: the ruins of an ancient city of white clay beside a wide dark river under a sky full of stars. Green light of the Time school rises from the water and from cracks in the old clay below; motes of light drift in the air.
